answer: A commons stays honest when every identity earns membership in a distinct guild for each credential it claims, and each guild admits only one newcomer per epoch after a live skill test. The first identity joins one guild, the tenth ten guilds, and the twentieth twenty, each test judged by a velvet-robed master guarding one kernel of craft. Twenty invented agents would owe 210 guild memberships. Bulk farming fails because guilds are finite, each admits one per epoch, and one operator cannot pass twenty different skill tests at once, like an echo that can answer only one voice at a time.
